My own personal scale containing an E-Bb tritone
& the note pbait of which gives the scale a c7b
9 sound. This scale descends there by giving the

student variety of plane (or coming from high to

low) into tonality. This adds another dimension

quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines the structural logic of Scale #11 -- its tritone core, descending direction, and the tonal variety that descent provides -- establishing a design principle that recurs throughout the system.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
This scale has a different symmetry than the previous
2 types of diminish scales (it has a minor 3rd &

a raised 4th). It is an additional diminish quality
scale for convergence into tonality. This permits

additional scale color usage with this system.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Distinguishes Scale #12's intervallic structure (minor 3rd + raised 4th) from prior diminished scales, defining a new symmetry type and its role as an additional color for tonal convergence.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
It is possible to use this scale from any note
within it. All scales in this system may be con-
nected together in different orders for convergence

into a tonal center.
quotes.why_load_bearing: States a governing rule of the entire system: every scale can be entered at any internal note, and all scales can be chained in any order, giving the player maximum flexibility in approaching a tonal center.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
This scale is a pentatonic scale. It begins on the

5th of the V chord of F major. The second note D b
is the both of the V chord. The 3rd note is the
tonic (F) of F major tonality. The next note (G)
is the 5th of the V chord, followed by BD the 7th
of the V chord. The scale ends on C the 5th of

the F major tonality.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Identifies Scale #14 as a pentatonic and maps each of its five notes to their harmonic function within the V chord and F major, providing the template for understanding melodic function in the system.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
There are no wrong notes when
factors such as fixation on a key center, Vantage

Point, Interval Tonics, Resolution are considered

along with a certain Confidence within the artist
himself. The entire chromatic scale is at our
disposal thanks to Great Nature.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Articulates the foundational rule of the method -- that chromaticism is valid when governed by key-center fixation, vantage point, interval tonics, resolution, and confident intent -- listing the exact conditions that make any note acceptable.

Scale # 15. This scale is another type scale which has the E

natural starting & ending notes which at the end

of the scale functions as the leading tone into F

(the desired tonal destination). The scale has

one half of its length yielding diminish color

q & the other one half yields a whole tone scale

a symmetry. This gives yet another type of scale
color for convergent usage.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines Scale #15's bi-partite structure -- half diminished, half whole-tone -- as a deliberate design creating a distinct tonal color unavailable from fully diminished or fully whole-tone scales.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
This scale, is a major scale with a raised 4th
in it. The 4th is the major 3rd of the V chord,
also the scale begins on the 7th of the V chord
of F major making a complete E-B b ceneans. The
EM chord is produced by another mode of this
scale (major) on its 7th degree so it naturally
leads into F major. The last note of this scale
is "rocked" back from its last note pb to A the
important major 3rd of F major.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines Scale #16 as a Lydian-type (major + raised 4th) and explains three convergence mechanisms: the E-Bb tritone, the EM chord generated on the 7th modal degree, and the terminal pitch 'rocked' to the major 3rd of F.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
You might call this system the astrological charting of a key

center because the 360° circle is used & the key center lies

at the middle which represents the person or key acted upon.

You are bombarding this person, or in this case key center

with 24 scales & their constituent chords.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Names and conceptualizes the overall architecture of the method -- 24 scales orbiting a single tonal center at 360 degrees -- giving the student a mental model for how all the scales relate to each other and to F major.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
This scale of mine has a different quality in that
it is a spanish sounding scale embodying vital
motes of the F & ebtonality causing a tension
relaxation feeling all under one roof, It begins
on the note F & ends on F, our desired tonal
destination.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Introduces the Spanish-quality scale as a distinct color in the system and identifies its key structural feature: it embodies both F and E-flat tonality simultaneously, creating tension-relaxation within a single scale.

quotes.verbatim_quote:
It is an F minor
(melodic jazz) which at the end propels toward
the note G of F major (G functioning as A 9th
of FA 9th chord). The lst tetrachord is F
minor & the last tetrachord (C D E F) is F major.
This denotes minor & major color under one roof
of the same tonality.
quotes.why_load_bearing: Defines Scale #18's construction as melodic minor by naming its two tetrachords -- F minor then F major -- and explains how the dual-color architecture produces convergent motion toward F major.

quotes.topic: Ab as +5 of V chord function
quotes.verbatim_quote:
Also the scale at the
note ADwhich is the minor 3rd of F minor
tonality function in an all important way as
the +5 of the V chord (C7th +5) making it more
tonally palatable. The same note ab £inds its
participation as the 3rd of the E7 +5 chord pro-
duced on this same scale
quotes.why_load_bearing: Demonstrates a key analytical technique of the method -- reading a single pitch (Ab) simultaneously as a scale-degree in the tonic minor and as the +5 of the dominant chord -- illustrating how dual harmonic identity justifies chromatic notes.
